raw_extraction.source_limitations: This document describes identified risks and ongoing research without specifying causation, efficacy, or clinical approval. All claims are observational and based on current understanding. No specific biomarkers, dosages, or treatment protocols are provided. The environment is not explicitly defined beyond spaceflight contexts. No data on recovery timelines or thresholds are included.

entities.description: Stresses of spaceflight can awaken inactive viruses, leading to rashes and other symptoms.
entities.evidence_text: The stresses of spaceflight can awaken inactive viruses inside the bodies of astronauts, leading to rashes and other symptoms.

entities.description: Astronauts experience motion sickness, hand-eye or gait coordination issues, and dizziness during gravitational changes.
entities.evidence_text: Astronauts can experience motion sickness, issues with hand-eye or gait coordination, and dizziness during gravitational changes, making it difficult to walk or operate a vehicle.

entities.description: Weightlessness alters blood circulation and heart/blood vessel function, potentially increasing cardiovascular event risk.
entities.evidence_text: Weightlessness alters blood circulation and how the heart and blood vessels function, potentially increasing the risk of cardiovascular events.

entities.description: Transitioning from pressurized spacecraft to lower-pressure spacesuit causes complications when dissolved nitrogen bubbles in body tissues.
entities.evidence_text: Transitioning from a pressurized spacecraft to a lower-pressure spacesuit can cause health and mission complications when dissolved nitrogen starts to bubble within body tissues.

entities.description: Skin and gut microbiomes change in space, potentially increasing crew illness risk.
entities.evidence_text: Skin and gut microbiomes can change in space, potentially increasing the risk of crew members getting sick.
